remediation_v4.purpose: Repair the REAL runtime break created when MT-109 correctly removed the unauthenticated unscoped flight-recorder routes: the mounted native app could no longer write its own Flight Recorder events.

token_contract.which: The token field of the canonical on-disk binding at crate::mcp::binding_path() - the exact file handshake_core capture_context reads. The in-process mcp_token was DELIBERATELY not used: if another instance republished the canonical file, the in-process copy is stale while the backend only consults the file.
token_contract.refresh: No cache. Re-read on EVERY request, resolved as late as possible inside the async POST body on the off-frame dispatch worker (never the egui frame thread). Publication is an atomic replace, so a rebind with a new port/token/owning process is picked up by the very next event with no invalidation logic.
token_contract.absence: Typed EmitError::MissingSessionBinding{path,reason}; the POST is NOT attempted. It lands in the shared ErrorRing and renders as flight-recorder.emit-error-{index} with an AccessKit value, and record_emit_failure_diagnostic gets a distinct Tier-2 kind. A rejected credential is EmitError::SessionRejected{status,error_code} carrying the exact HSK-4xx-FR-* code. Never a silent drop.
token_contract.identity: build_post_body now OMITS actor_id, actor_kind and workspace_id entirely - the path segment carries the workspace, the binding carries the actor, and the server fills both. event.actor_id/event.workspace_id remain local routing and diagnostic identity only.

spec_basis: Master Spec v02.206 §2.3.13.12.3 Authorization law (7): "Denials MUST use constant-shape responses where practical so counts, identifiers, names, paths, thumbnails, timing, search facets, error variants, logs, or diagnostics do not reveal that a restricted resource exists." (02-system-architecture.md)

Master Spec v02.206 §2.3.13.12.3 (2)+(6): every request authorizes Principal+session+action+exact resource; deny-by-default on every executable backend boundary. §2.3.13.12.4: Flight Recorder tables are protected resources and cannot become side-channel bypasses.
Codex [CX-132C] HARD_DENY_BY_DEFAULT_ACROSS_ALL_BOUNDARIES: missing/invalid/stale session context MUST deny (satisfied by both codes; does not choose the number).

The spec does NOT pin the numeric HTTP status for a missing credential; it pins the SHAPE (constant, non-distinguishing). A distinct 401 variant ahead of the protected-resource layer would be a second denial shape.
product_basis: src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/flight_recorder.rs::authorize_flight_recorder_request (line ~370) routes EVERY recorder request through api/authority.rs::authorize_request, which returns constant_denial() = 403 {error: HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE} for missing token, malformed token, missing channel binding, broker denial, and capability denial alike. unauthenticated_recorder() (401 HSK-401-FR-SESSION, flight_recorder.rs:96) is no longer reachable on that path.

The backend in-crate tests already pin the constant denial for the no-credential case: flight_recorder.rs ~4276 asserts "POST runtime_chat_event without binding" -> StatusCode::FORBIDDEN + HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE "must use the constant protected-resource denial"; ~4970 asserts unscoped/blank-scope reads -> 403 HSK-403-PROTECTED-RESOURCE.

This is NOT the spec-silent branch: §2.3.13.12.3(7) governs the denial shape, and the product authority layer plus its own pinned tests implement it.
